transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-14 11:00 PT / 14:00 ET, Duration ~52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Patel (Redwood SE), Noah Li (Redwood SE), Lena Park (SignalForge Head of ML), Marco Ruiz (CTO), Samir Iqbal (Lead Data Eng), Ava Gomez (Product)

Summary: Quick discovery focused on embeddings dimensionality, throughput targets, vector DB integration (SignalForge uses a mix of PGVector + Milvus in staging), and tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated and Private (VPC) delivery. Candidate pilot: 50–100k docs initially, scale plan to 5–10M vectors.

Topics: embeddings dims (128/768/1536), hybrid retrieval+rerank pipeline, batch sizing and latency SLOs, sharding for vector DB, KV cache and prefix caching, security (SOC2/KMS), pricing model (per-token vs reserved), benchmarking plan.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. Quick intros?
[00:00:10] Lena: Hi, Lena here. Head of ML at SignalForge. We're building a customer search/insights product, and wanna move away from slower heuristic search to embeddings + rerank.
[00:00:20] Marco: Marco, CTO. Main concerns are throughput and cost — we have 2000 QPS during peak for search API, which is... (laughs) non-trivial.
[00:00:30] Samir: Samir — data eng. I own ETL and vector pipeline, we currently batch embed nocturnally but want near-real time.
[00:00:40] Omar: Omar, Redwood SE. We'll try to map tradeoffs and options. Quick note: we often see customers start with hosted and then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput.
[00:00:50] Ava: Ava, PM — timeline is pilot in Q2, production H2.

[00:01:30] Maya: Great. High level — what's your current embedding stack? I saw a doc that said PGVector + Milvus in staging, can you confirm?
[00:01:40] Samir: Yes, we spin up Milvus clusters for larger jobs. For quick lookups we use PGVector on RDS but it's getting slow at scale. The embeddings dims are mixed — older models 768, new pipeline pushes 1,536 for better relevance.
[00:01:55] Lena: We have about 600k vectors today, expected growth to ~6M by year end.

[00:03:00] Omar: Okay, that's a useful baseline. A few common knobs: embedding dimensionality vs index size, reranker complexity (a cross-encoder vs light weight scorer), and host choices. For throughput: are you targeting sub-200ms for the first-pass search or is 500-800ms acceptable if rerank is async?
[00:03:20] Marco: Ideally sub-250ms end-to-end for user-facing search. We can do async for heavy tasks but primary search should feel instant.

[00:04:10] Noah: Quick interruption — when you say first-pass, do you mean ANN search latency only, or includes the embedding call?
[00:04:20] Samir: We'll do embeddings precomputed for most docs; queries need live user embedding which is <50ms target.

[00:05:00] Maya: Good, so design looks like: query->embed (client or Redwood API) -> ANN (PGVector/Milvus) -> top-K -> rerank on Redwood Hosted/Dedicated. We often recommend reusing Redwood for embeddings to consolidate ops, but many choose off-host embedding exporter. Any restrictions on customer data leaving VPC?
[00:05:20] Marco: Security is big. SOC2 required, plus we want KMS for keys and option to run Private in our AWS account for classified clients.
[00:05:30] Omar: We support SOC2, SSO/SAML, and Private deployments (VPC). For KMS you can use your own CMK in Dedicated/Private.

[00:06:20] Lena: On rerank model: we'd like a two-stage approach — lexical/hybrid retrieval for recall, then a cross-encoder re-ranker. The cross-encoder can be run in smaller batch sizes but it's expensive. Thoughts?
[00:06:40] Omar: That's typical. For cost/perf we recommend limiting rerank to top 50 results and using a quantized rerank model or a small fine-tuned model. Also Redwood supports a dynamic fallback: if Dedicated capacity is exhausted, we fall back to hosted smaller variant.
[00:07:00] Marco: How deterministic is that fallback? We can't have degraded results silently.
[00:07:10] Maya: We have rollout and fallback policies in the console. We'll annotate results and provide tracing so you can detect quality drift and opt into alerts.

[00:08:00] Samir: Let's talk numbers. If we run 2k QPS at peak, with a top-50 rerank and embeddings precomputed, what's the expected GPU footprint on Dedicated?
[00:08:20] Omar: Very approximate: for a small cross-encoder quantized to int8, you might get ~300-400 qps per GPU depending on sequence length and batching. That implies a pool of 6–8 GPUs for 2k qps, but we would design autoscaling and batching to smooth bursts. If you use a larger reranker you need more.
[00:09:00] Lena: Sequence length for reranker is usually 256 tokens average.
[00:09:10] Omar: That helps. Also batching across concurrent requests increases throughput but can add 10–30ms. We can configure max latency SLO to cap batch windows.

[00:10:15] Noah: On vector DB sharding: when you hit millions of vectors, Milvus/Pinecone do sharding but we advise horizontal ANN shards co-located with inference for locality. If you opt for Redwood Private, we can place inference near your Milvus cluster to reduce network hops.
[00:10:40] Marco: Is there a recommended index type? HNSW vs IVF?
[00:10:50] Omar: HNSW is popular for recall/latency sweet spot, but memory-heavy. IVF+PQ is denser and cheaper but you must tune recall thresholds. Depends on dim (1536 favors PQ).

[00:12:00] Lena: On embedding dims—does Redwood have guidance? We're torn between 768 and 1536 — cost/accuracy tradeoff is unclear.
[00:12:10] Maya: We run evals per workload. 768 often is sufficient for many QA/search tasks; 1536 gives gains especially for fine-grained semantic similarity. But storage and ANN memory cost roughly doubles. For a 6M vector corpus, moving to 1536 increases index RAM by a lot. You might do hybrid: use 768 for broad retrieval and 1536 for reranking or special namespaces.
[00:12:45] Samir: Interesting — mixed dims complicates index. Is it feasible to keep two parallel indexes?
[00:12:55] Omar: It's feasible but adds complexity. Another pattern: store high-dim embeddings offline and compute query-side transformations—embedding compression or product quantization on the index. We can share sample config for that.

[00:14:00] Marco: What's the integration path — do we push vectors to Redwood, or keep them in our DB and call Redwood for rerank only?
[00:14:10] Maya: Both possible. Hosted flows often push embeddings to your vector DB while using Redwood for on-the-fly embeddings and rerank. Private/Dedicated allows you to keep vectors in your VPC and run inference next to them. We'll map a pilot with minimal data exfiltration.

[00:15:20] Lena: Benchmark: we want a pilot with 50k docs, 5k daily queries, 30 QPS peak, and then a load test to 2k qps. Can Redwood help run the load test?
[00:15:30] Omar: Yes — we can provision a short Dedicated pool for benchmark or run hosted benchmark with instrumentation. We'll need your sample queries and queries-per-second profile.

[00:16:40] Maya: Security asks — do you have specific compliance docs you need?
[00:16:45] Marco: SOC2 + data residency notes. For certain customers, we must guarantee data doesn't leave eu-west. Also SAML integration for our internal team.
[00:16:55] Maya: We have SOC2 reports and EU region deployments, and we support SAML SSO setup. We'll attach the security pack.

[00:18:10] Samir: A few practical items — ingest cadence, re-embedding when documents change, and vector TTL. We're thinking daily reindex for docs changed within 24 hours. Latency requirement for new docs to appear is <5 minutes ideally.
[00:18:25] Omar: For near-real time ingestion you can use our streaming ingest or push via API — under Dedicated we can support very low-latency ingestion and indexing pipelines. For 5-minute visibility, design a small fast pipeline: embed on write and write to index with small batch.

[00:19:40] Lena: Cost question: how do token-based model costs map to rerank? We're concerned about runaway costs when reranker is cross-encoder.
[00:19:50] Maya: Rerank is billed by inference unit — in Hosted it's per-token/per-request; in Dedicated you buy reserved GPUs and pay less per inference. We'll run cost estimates for your QPS and model choice. Also caching top queries and KV cache can reduce repeated rerank calls. Note — KV cache sometimes transcribed as KV 'cash' in our notes, hope that's not confusing.

[00:21:00] Noah: On caching: Redwood supports prefix/KV cache to serve repeated prefixes or popular queries from memory. It reduces both latency and cost. We'll show example hit-rate numbers from customers.

[00:22:10] Marco: What about model selection — open models vs Redwood curated ones. We have IP concerns and prefer open models but want performance.
[00:22:25] Omar: We maintain a catalog of open models optimized for inference and verified profiles. For cross-encoder rerankers you can fine-tune an open model and we profile for latency. Quantization to int8 or int4 often helps.

[00:23:40] Lena: Hybrid search: we want to combine lexical BM25 with vector scoring. Any recommended scoring blending?
[00:23:50] Omar: A common approach is rank fusion: score_norm * alpha + lexical_score * (1-alpha). We usually tune alpha on validation queries. Redwood Optimize can run quality regression checks against a labeled set.

[00:25:05] Samir: Operational concerns — circuit breakers, graceful degradation. If the rerank fails, we need deterministic fallback (e.g., only ANN results).
[00:25:15] Maya: We provide fallback policies; you can require a minimum confidence and failover to a fallback model or route to cached results. We also expose per-request tracing so you can monitor QoE.

[00:26:40] Marco: Pricing for Dedicated — committed monthly vs burstable? What's typical for 6–8 GPUs?
[00:26:50] Maya: Committed monthly with burst credits. We'll put numbers in the spreadsheet, but expect an order-of-magnitude lower per-inference cost vs hosted at high volume. We'll include a TCO spreadsheet.

[00:28:30] Noah: For the pilot we recommend: Hosted minimal (embeddings + small rerank) to validate relevance, then Dedicated pilot with a small GPU pool for throughput validation, then Private for customer-managed VPC if needed.

[00:29:20] Lena: That path sounds sensible. Any gotchas we should be aware of?
[00:29:30] Omar: Watch out for index memory growth with high dims, cold-start latency on scale-ups, and network egress if vectors move across regions. We'll provide sample configs to mitigate.

[00:31:00] Samir: Can you share an example config for batching settings? We want to avoid large batching that adds 100ms but also want throughput.
[00:31:10] Omar: We'll share a config showing batch window 8–12ms and max batch size tuned to keep P99 under your SLO. Also show quantization knobs.

[00:32:40] Maya: Let's capture next steps — we'll send pricing and security docs and set up a benchmark window. Any questions about data residency?
[00:32:55] Marco: We want EU-only for some customers.
[00:33:00] Maya: Noted — we'll include region options.

[00:34:20] Lena: Small detail: metadata handling — we index different namespaces per customer; will Redwood support metadata filters in ANN?
[00:34:30] Omar: Yes, Redwood's routing supports filtering by metadata and namespace. When using a third-party vector DB you can apply metadata filters at query time. We'll demo that in the pilot.

[00:36:00] Noah: Another point — embeddings versioning. We recommend storing version tags on vectors and re-running quality checks after model updates.
[00:36:10] Lena: Makes sense. We'll want an automated eval whenever embeddings version changes.

[00:37:30] Marco: Anything else from Redwood side?
[00:37:40] Noah: We'll include a benchmark plan: dataset, query set, load profile, metrics (latency P50/P95/P99, recall@k, cost per Q).

[00:38:20] Samir: For the load test, do you recommend synthetic queries or production traffic replay?
[00:38:30] Omar: Replay of production traffic is best for fidelity; synthetic is OK for stress testing. We'll accept either.

[00:40:00] Maya: Ok, recap. Action items: we'll send pricing + security pack, Omar sends batching + quantization config, and you (Lena) deliver sample dataset. We'll schedule a 2-hour benchmark kickoff next week.
[00:40:20] Marco: Confirmed.

[00:41:10] Ava: Timeline: after benchmark we aim for a two-week pilot then decision meeting.

[00:42:00] Maya: Any final q's?
[00:42:10] Lena: One — can you provide a rough cost per 1k queries for hosted with a small reranker?
[00:42:20] Maya: We'll put numbers in the spreadsheet. Roughly higher than Dedicated per 1k at scale; but for pilot Hosted may be cheaper turnkey.

[00:43:00] Noah: We'll also include notes on running rerank as a batched microservice vs per-request.

[00:44:20] Samir: Thanks — appreciate the practical guidance. Minor transcription note: earlier you said 'RV fallback' — meant 'runtime fallback', just clarifying.
[00:44:30] Omar: Yep, runtime fallback.

[00:45:00] (small chatter, scheduling link posted)
[00:46:30] Maya: We'll share link to security docs and calendar invite. Thanks everyone.
[00:46:45] Lena: Thanks, this was helpful.
[00:47:00] Marco: Thank you.
[00:47:10] (meeting ends)

--- End transcript ---
